identity.title: Evidence of Fast Pebble Growth Near Condensation Fronts in the HL Tau Protoplanetary Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we analyze ALMA long baseline 2.9, 1.3 and 0.87 mm continuum images of the young star HL Tau
More detailed descriptions of the data and calibration can be found in APR

question.value: Are the dark rings (emission dips) in the ALMA HL Tau continuum images due to fast pebble growth near condensation fronts of abundant volatiles?

evidence.quote: Here we propose that the dark concentric rings observed in the (sub)mm interferometry of HL Tau are due to fast pebble growth near condensation fronts.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data sets: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.
The ALMA Band 3, 6 and 7 (or wavelengths of 2.9, 1.3 and 0.87 mm, respectively) HL Tau observations were carried out in 2014
With longest baselines of 15.2 km, the HL Tau observations achieved exceptional spatial resolution

used_for.value: Deprojecting visibilities, imaging, CLEAN nterms=2 spectral index map

evidence.quote: use CASA v4.3 (cite: McMullin07) to deproject the visibility data and generate synthesized images for all three bands
The 63 AU dip is resolved at all bands, with a FWHM of 17-18 AU.

results_numeric.quantity: Dip minimum relative to smooth continuum

evidence.quote: The minimum surface intensity of the dips range from 37% to 78% that of the smooth continuum from the best-fit models.

results_numeric.quantity: Spectral index inside 48 AU, peaks at 13 and 32 AU dips

evidence.quote: inside of 48 AU $\alpha$$\sim$2, except for increases to values of $\sim$2.6 and $\sim$2.4 at the 13 AU and 32 AU dips, respectively

results_numeric.quantity: Surface density needed for tau_1.3mm = 1 at 48 AU

evidence.quote: a surface density of $\Sigma_{\rm gas}$=100  g cm$^{-2}$  at 48 AU is needed to reach $\tau_{\rm 1.3\,mm}$ = 1

findings_qualitative.value: Water ice water-line is at <4-5 AU from brightness temperature, unresolved; dips overlap condensation fronts of water (13 AU), NH3/hydrates (32 AU), CO2 and CO/N2 clathrates (63 AU) using the MFH profile

evidence.quote: pure water condenses around the 13 AU dip, while pure NH$_3$ or ammonia (and hydrogen sulfide) hydrates condense around the 32 AU dip.

claims.hypothesis: The three prominent dips coincide with condensation fronts of abundant volatiles
claims.experiment: Fit dip centers in deprojected profiles and compare to computed condensation temperatures and the MFH mid-plane profile
claims.result: Dips at ~13, 32, 63 AU overlap the fronts of water, ammonia/hydrates, and CO2/CO and N2 clathrates
claims.finding: Dip locations are coincident with expected condensation fronts

evidence.quote: the location of the three most prominent dips in the HL Tau (sub)mm interferometric images are coincident with the expected condensation fronts of the main volatiles

claims.hypothesis: Spectral index variation in the dips indicates rapid pebble growth
claims.experiment: Spectral index map from bands 6 and 7 and a two-population dust opacity model
claims.result: alpha ~2 inside 48 AU with increases at the 13 and 32 AU dips; model with decimeter-size second population reproduces this
claims.finding: Most dust mass resides in decimeter-size pebbles inside the dips

evidence.quote: we infer that most of the dust mass needs to reside in a population that has grown to decimeter size scales inside the 13 and 32 AU dips

why_this_method.value: Deprojected circular images make a one-parameter radial brightness function

evidence.quote: For our purposes, it is much easier to work on deprojected, circular images.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Optically thick inner disk with optically thin dips rejected: requires massive disk and brightness temperature conflicts with SED-derived temperature

evidence.quote: This explanation faces two difficulties. First, a massive disk is needed to create optically thick mm-continuum with modest grain growth.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single dust size distribution with beta~0 disfavored

evidence.quote: for a single dust size-distribution, $\alpha>2$ within the 13/32 AU dips demands smaller dust (and reduced mass surface densities) at these radii.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust model is only an order-of-magnitude estimate; other condensation fronts' growth rates are unmodeled

evidence.quote: It is unclear if pebble growth is sufficiently rapid around other condensation fronts to explain the HL Tau results.

referee_caveats_inferred: Correlation between dip radii and condensation fronts depends on the adopted MFH temperature profile with large uncertainty
Coincidence of three dips with many species' fronts is weakly constraining
Two-population model is not fit and parameters are fixed by hand; alternatives like unresolved optical depth or scattering not explored
Spectral index relies on unspecified flux calibration accuracy between bands

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data sets: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.
